check_service_status.description: Check whether Random-d.uk is up and handing out ducks, and how quickly. This is the one action that reports a problem as a value instead of failing the step, so a workflow can decide what to do about it. Answering at all and answering with a duck are reported separately, because a parked domain does the first and not the second.

mock_response.message: Random-d.uk is up and handing out ducks (172.7 ms for /api/v2/random).

check_service_status.name: check_service_status

byte_size.description: How many bytes the site answered with.

content_type.description: The media type the site answered with, application/json when it is handing out ducks.

image_url.description: The picture the check itself was given, so a green check comes with a duck. Null when the site answered without one.

message.description: A one-line summary of the result.

online.description: True when the site answered with a duck. This is the field to branch on.

reachable.description: True when the site answered at all, whatever it said.

response_time_ms.description: How long the request took, in milliseconds.

status_code.description: The HTTP status the site answered with, or null when it could not be reached.

count_ducks.description: Find out how many ducks Random-d.uk has right now, across the photos, the GIFs and the HTTP status codes, and which photo is the newest. The collection grows as people send more ducks in. Use it to pin a seeded pick, to bound a duck number a workflow makes up, or to notice when new ducks have arrived. Two counts come back for the photos because the site reports two: duck_count is how many pictures there are, and file_count is the site's own tally of filenames, which is higher because it lists most pictures twice.
count_ducks.name: count_ducks

duck_count.description: How many distinct photos the site has. This is the number to quote and the one a seeded pick draws from. It goes up over time and never down.

file_count.description: The site's own image_count, which counts filenames rather than pictures: most photos are listed twice, once as n.jpg and once as n.JPG, and the two are the same picture. It runs about half again as high as duck_count, so do not report it as a number of ducks.

gif_count.description: How many distinct GIFs the site has.

gif_file_count.description: The site's own gif_count. The GIFs are listed once each, so this matches gif_count.

http_code_count.description: How many HTTP status codes have a duck of their own.

newest.description: The newest photo. They are numbered from 1 upwards, so it is the last one.

attribution.description: The credit the site asks to be shown with its pictures, normally 'Powered by random-d.uk'. On a random draw it is the site's own wording, taken from the answer itself.

content_type.description: The picture's media type, image/jpeg or image/gif.

duck_number.description: The duck's number, which is how a duck is named on this site: duck 449 is the picture at https://random-d.uk/api/v2/449.jpg, and it stays that duck for good. Keep it to fetch the same duck again later. Null for a duck that has no number: the HTTP status code ducks are filed under their code instead, and a random draw that came back with an address carrying no number leaves it empty.

get_duck_of_the_day.description: Pick a duck from a seed, so the same seed always picks the same duck. Seed with the date, which is the default, and a daily post that retries, or that two people run an hour apart, shows the same duck, while tomorrow shows a different one. Seed with a channel or a customer name instead and each one gets its own duck. The pick is over however many ducks the site has, so give a duck count to pin it: the collection grows, and a bigger collection means a different duck for the same seed.

get_http_duck.description: Get the duck that stands for an HTTP status code: a duck that is 404 Not Found, a duck that is 418 I'm a teapot. Wire in the status an earlier HTTP step came back with to illustrate an alert, a status page or a failure notice. The site has ducks for fifteen codes and the step reads the live list rather than a copy, so a code added later works the day it is added. description: Put a duck in your workflow with Random-d.uk, the free keyless picture site at random-d.uk: 559 duck photographs and 57 animations, and counting. Get one at random for a stand-up opener or a channel mascot, get a handful for a gallery, download one as a file to attach to an email, or get it inline as a data URI where a link will not load. It also keeps a duck for fifteen HTTP status codes, so an alert about a 404 or a 500 can carry the duck that stands for it. Every duck has a number, so a duck worth keeping can be fetched again exactly, and a seeded pick gives the same duck all day and a new one tomorrow.
